[measurement]{.chip .measured} [negative result]{.chip .negative} Entry 23 · milestone M3
:::

Dataset v3 samples where TORAX trajectories go, with whole runs kept out of training
([entry 22](22-dataset-v3-torax-trajectories.qmd)). The final ensembles have now been trained
on the broad v1/v2 data plus v3's training points. The monotone variants meet the owner's
held-out accuracy target on both machines: [MAST-U: Q_e 17.8%, Q_i 25.2%; ITER: Q_e 7.2%, Q_i 10.8%; all meet the 30% target]{.claim}[C-129](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-129){.cid .st-measured}.

An audit loaded the saved models, checked their metadata and dataset hashes, replayed the
trajectory split, and recomputed the scores. The v3 test set was never a training input.
This checks the implementation's reproducibility; it is not independent physics validation.

## Structure and its cost

Electron and ion heat fluxes are nonnegative in use. Each member is built so that its heat flux
cannot fall as its own temperature gradient rises, with the other inputs fixed. Recomputed
checks found [no negative member slopes on the tested v1/v3 points or scan grids, and no negative neighbour differences on the scan grids]{.claim}[C-130](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-130){.cid .st-tested}. Those sampled checks support the construction; proof over
the whole input domain belongs to M4.

TGLF itself is not always monotone. On the broad scans where its flux decreases, the final
models depart from it: [MAST-U: Q_e 3.14, Q_i 3.36; ITER: Q_e 2.51, Q_i 2.11 signed-log units]{.claim}[C-131](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-131){.cid .st-preliminary}. This includes approximation error as well as the
cost of imposing monotonicity. Passing the v3 median target does not remove that ceiling or
establish accuracy everywhere in the training box.

Clipping also does not identify every stable point. The exact-zero rates and uncalibrated
spread coverage are [mean ±2 standard deviations covers Q_e/Q_i at 75.3%/74.4% (MAST-U), 85.6%/80.8% (ITER); exact-zero predictions where TGLF is nonpositive: 44.0%/47.0% (MAST-U), 52.3%/21.1% (ITER)]{.claim}[C-137](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-137){.cid .st-measured}. Calibration and the guard's uncertainty policy remain
M4 work.

## Inside the loop

The comparison command now selects the final monotone v3 model explicitly. A local RAPTOR
L-mode run finished with [all profiles finite; no stalled or coarse-tolerance step; post-step guard rejection 33.1%; execution 1.62 s after compilation]{.claim}[C-135](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-135){.cid .st-measured}. Against the saved TGLF run at the same final
time, its profile differences are [T_e 7.72%, T_i 9.23%, n_e 11.36%, psi 0.32%]{.claim}[C-134](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-134){.cid .st-preliminary}. Electron and ion temperature agreement
improved relative to v1; density agreement did not. This is one case, not a closed-loop bound.

The strict derivative and discrete-balance checks exposed a stopping-precision limitation:
[v3 derivative discrepancy about 1.8e-5 relative; peak discrete energy residual 1.11e-5 (v1) and 1.36e-6 (v3)]{.claim}[C-140](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-140){.cid .st-tested}. Converging Newton more tightly, to `residual_tol=1e-10`, gives
[v1 and v3 pass: three-step derivative FD tolerance 1e-7, forward/reverse tolerance 1e-12; guard masks unchanged over the stencil]{.claim}[C-138](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-138){.cid .st-tested} and [v1 and v3 pass: energy residual below 1e-6 and particle residual below 1e-10, with fine solver convergence]{.claim}[C-139](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-139){.cid .st-tested}. The original assertion limits are retained.
The runner records the solver setting, and the default-tolerance limitation remains [K-026](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-026).

A second execution check, on ITER hybrid, gives [50 steps to 5 s, all four profiles finite, no stalled or coarse-tolerance steps; accepted-state guard rejection 26.9%]{.claim}[C-142](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-142){.cid .st-measured}. It checks coupled
execution and guard behavior, without a TGLF error bound.

The completed earlier timing comparison used v1. A fresh matched v3 comparison was submitted,
but the scheduler cancelled it before execution and produced no output. There is no matched
v3 speed-up measurement to report. The job script is prepared for a rerun once that compute
issue is resolved.

M3 remains in progress: the held-out transport target passes, while matched v3 timing,
broader coupled comparisons, and the RF and pedestal surrogate tasks remain open.
